blocks.content: A person shall not be qualified for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court unless he is a citizen of India.

rows: Must have served as a Judge of a High Court
Must have practiced as an Advocate of a High Court
Must be a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President

items: There is NO minimum age prescribed by the Constitution for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.
The provision allowing appointment of a 'distinguished jurist' exists under Article 124, though no such appointment has been made to date.
Experience requirements can be fulfilled across two or more High Courts in succession.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A candidate must be a citizen of India to qualify for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.
Requires either 5 years of experience as a High Court judge or 10 years of practice as a High Court advocate.
An eminent legal expert can be appointed under the category of a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.
The Constitution of India sets no minimum age limit for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court.
